purpose: Add the epistemic/provenance layer that the bounded byte-identical root migration receipt intentionally does not provide: classify how the two archived RAM prose fragments were created, compare their claims with later controlled project measurement and Linux primary documentation, and preserve them as negative/historical evidence rather than current technical truth.

migration_observed.boundary: This audit does not reopen or broaden the move. It evaluates the archived content's evidence status.

creation_provenance.introducing_commit_shape: The same commit created both executable-looking root-name fragments plus research_entity/topic_packets/fallback-runs/paket-1787844213500-ea6d28/ANTWORT.md; the fragments are portions of the answer text, not verified runtime receipts.

fragment_claims: malloc_trim after each generate returns approximately 379 MB
malloc_trim is O(1) and typically below 0.1 ms
Shared_Clean model-weight pages can be returned with MADV_FREE or MADV_DONTNEED and faulted back unchanged

project_measurement_comparison.scope: single idle-window/resume cycle, 3 trimmed + 3 control processes; not full coordinated 10-node fabric
project_measurement_comparison.reason: The observed trim effect is substantial but approximately 97 MB, not a demonstrated approximately-379-MB return; the controlled receipt does not establish the fragment's sub-millisecond trim/wake constants.

malloc_trim.supported: malloc_trim attempts to release free heap memory and reports whether memory was actually released

madvise.documented_constraint: MADV_FREE applies to private anonymous pages; once reclaimed, later references observe zero-fill-on-demand pages
madvise.implication: The fragment does not establish that Shared_Clean/file-backed model-weight pages can be MADV_FREE'd and transparently restored unchanged. A different eligible anonymous-memory design would need exact evidence.

artifacts.falsifier: Exact source/runtime-bound evidence reproduces the claimed approximately-379-MB release, sub-0.1-ms trim, 2-8-ms wake, and safe unchanged-weight MADV_FREE behavior under an eligible mapping design.

fragment_claims: Private_Dirty fell from approximately 379 MB to below 50 MB/process

artifacts.external_primary_constraint: Linux MADV_FREE is restricted to private anonymous mappings and can discard stale data; after reclaim, reads see zero-fill-on-demand until rewritten.
artifacts.falsifier: A source/hash-bound experiment demonstrates the claimed MADV_FREE memory floor, latency, and ten-process GRID10 correctness under an eligible mapping design.

cross_artifact_finding.finding: Git provenance shows the two executable-looking filenames were emitted as split answer fragments by one harness/aider documentation commit. This is a concrete file-output hygiene failure mode: model/tool output boundaries can become repository filenames.
cross_artifact_finding.engineering_consequence: AI/harness writers should bind writes to an explicit allowed path set and flag generated code-like filenames unless explicitly requested. Existing-file edits should additionally follow the current preimage-bound patch/scope-preservation contract.
cross_artifact_finding.falsifier: A contemporaneous task contract or functional consumer proves those exact odd root filenames were intentional durable interfaces.

coordination.nonduplication: Those artifacts establish path/reference/move scope. This v2 contributes provenance plus claim-vs-measurement/primary-source epistemic classification and does not duplicate the move authority.
